The ideaThe modelWhat this leaves out

The idea

A spring can make a camera or interface element feel responsive, heavy, or slightly out of control. This study isolates the damping ratio so the difference is easy to see.

The curve shows the whole response. “Run response” follows that same curve over three seconds. Nothing animates until you ask it to.

The model

The spring starts at position 0, at rest. Its target moves instantly to 1. Natural frequency stays fixed at 9 radians per second; only damping changes.

Inspect the equation
x″ + 2ζωx′ + ω²x = ω²
x(0) = 0, x′(0) = 0
ω = 9 rad/s

The plot uses the analytic solution, rather than integrating a simulation each frame. Its position therefore doesn’t depend on the display’s refresh rate.

Read the damping reference →

What this leaves out

This is a one-dimensional, linear spring with a fixed target. It doesn’t model collisions, changing targets, or a real game camera. A three-second window also doesn’t mean every setting has settled.
